title: AI job titles: which titles that name AI or machine learning employers post, counted on company job boards
source: The job index of ATS Jobs Search (Apify Actor scaleturn/ats-jobs-search), built 2026-11-19T04:03:40.394Z: 23287 company job boards on six applicant tracking systems.

method.ai_named: A title names AI when it contains one of these terms. Case-sensitive, not touching a Latin letter or digit: AI, A.I., ML, LLM, LLMs, KI, NLP. Any case: machine learning, artificial intelligence, künstliche intelligenz, deep learning, genai, gen ai, generative ai, computer vision, natural language processing, large language model, mlops, llmops, aiops, agentic, prompt engineer. In a title written all in capitals, a short form counts only at the start or end of the title or of one of its parts, or next to an English job word. In a title that names law, a legal role or tax, LLM is the Master of Laws degree and does not count.
method.role_name: Titles are split into parts at spaced dashes, bars, commas, colons, @ and brackets; a part that is only seniority words (as in 'Senior / Staff') is skipped. The role name is the first part with gender tags, leading seniority words (Senior, Sr., Staff, Principal, Lead, Junior, Jr., Founding, Mid-level, Entry-level, Distinguished, Expert) and trailing levels (I-V, 1-5) removed and slashes closed up, read case-insensitively with hyphens as spaces and abbreviations as their full form (ML: machine learning; A.I. and artificial intelligence: AI; GenAI: generative AI; a slash pair such as AI/ML stays as written). When the first part names AI, the AI term is in the role name; otherwise it is in a suffix (a team, product or project) and the first part is the role.

training.label: AI training and data work
training.rule: \bAI[- ]?trainers?\b|\btrainers? network\b|\bAI[- ]?tutors?\b|annotat|\bdata contributors?\b|\b(?:research|recording|training|voice|conversation|video) contributors?\b|\bAI training\b(?! (?:infra|platform|system|cluster|compute|framework|engineer|runtime|stack|data platform))|\bAI (?:speech )?testers?\b|\bspeech tester\b|evaluators? for AI|\bresearch participants?\b|\bstudy participants?\b|\brecord(?:ing)? videos?\b|\bdata collection operator\b|\bteleoperator\b|\brobot trainer\b|\bAI data (?:specialist|quality|annotator|associate)|\bKI-Tester\b|\braters?\b

customer.label: Customer-facing and consulting
customer.rule: forward[- ]deployed|\bsolutions? (?:engineer|architect|consultant|specialist)|\bdeployment strategist\b|\bdeployment (?:lead|manager|specialist)\b|\bdelivery (?:lead|manager)\b|\bsales engineer\b|\bcustomer engineer\b|\bpre-?sales\b|\bconsult(?:ant|ing)\b|\bimplementation\b|\btechnical account\b|\bcustomer success\b|\badvisor\b|\bberater\b|\bapplied AI architect\b

method.groups_order: A title gets the first group whose rule matches anywhere in it; titles that match none are Other roles.
method.seniority: Junior when the title has a junior, intern, student or graduate word; else senior when it has Senior, Sr., Staff, Principal, Lead, Distinguished, Head of, Director, VP, Chief or Founding ('Member of Technical Staff' and 'Chief of Staff' are not seniority).
method.guide_titles: Titles that career guides and essays list, each matched against the role name (the first part, normalized as above) of every open title, AI-named or not; the variants matched are listed with each.
method.copies: A job with the same title, location and posting time on two or more boards of one ATS is counted once, on the board that lists it most often (as on the posting-day page).
method.region: From the location text, with ct-002/build_data.py's rule: US, Europe, or other (another region, several regions, or no place recognised).
method.boards: Boards, not companies: a company can run more than one board.
